purpose: Cycle 23 M4: ask L2's named question — do morphologically recurrent families trace to common ancestors, or converge from different founder lines? (Evolution Q3.) The question is reshaped first, because asking it across runs is not well posed.

closed_states: L2's named question is asked for the first time, with the family rule and the founder rule both IMPORTED from the instruments that own them
the null is MEASURED by permutation with both marginals preserved, so 'more than chance' has an operational meaning
single-member families are excluded and counted rather than averaged in at a structural 1.0

E5's stated reason for using descriptor clustering instead of ancestry (the WFC parent path carrying no single parent) is retired by DR 0042's adopted constrained layer, which records ancestry on every candidate
the committed E5 recurrent-family count is READ from the artifact, not quoted from prose that has gone stale
blocked_states: Asking whether recurrent families share ancestry ACROSS runs is not well posed, and that is a structural fact rather than a budget limit: every run builds its own bootstrap population, so a founder id in one run is not the same object as a founder id in another and the ancestry spaces are disjoint. Families recur MORPHOLOGICALLY; their ancestry cannot recur, because there is no shared ancestor pool for it to recur in. The question is therefore asked WITHIN each run and its answer compared across runs.

the statistic covers EVERY family in each run with >= 2 members, not only the families common to all runs. Review flagged the mismatch against the report's 'recurrent families' framing and it is real but bounded: the intersection here is 63 while the runs carry 63/64/64 families, so at most ONE non-recurrent family per run enters the mean and its null. It is recorded rather than re-scored — restricting the statistic after seeing the numbers is exactly the re-scoring this repo forbids (M1's size-matched-control precedent), and the verdict is not close to its bar at z +21.39 / +15.96 / +17.39. A recurrent-only variant is named for whoever runs it next

'convergent' is the NULL: it is an absence of evidence for common descent, never positive proof of convergence. The positive evidence is the distinct-founder count, reported separately and never folded into the verdict

a coarse family is E5's 4x4x4 cell, which is a descriptor region rather than a visually-verified morphological type; whether members of one cell look alike to a human is the owner-deferred survey's question and no proxy is offered
DR 0046's comparability rule applies: these descriptors are incumbent-geometry addresses and may not be read against probe-geometry counts

decision.rule: pre-registered (cycle 23 M4): the statistic is the mean largest-founder share over families with >= 2 members (single-member families excluded and counted — their share is 1.0 by construction). The null is MEASURED by permuting founder labels across elites, preserving both family sizes and founder-line sizes so the null differs from the observation only in the pairing. Verdict 'common_descent' when the observed share stands >= 2.0 standard deviations above that null, 'convergent' otherwise. 'convergent' IS THE NULL — an absence of evidence for common descent, never positive proof of convergence; the positive evidence is reported separately as the mean number of distinct founder lines per family.
